assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_criteria_id on the seed is 7)
HR Service Desk is user_group 4; no case_visibility criterion on the seed names it (the four existing ones, 1, 5, 6 and 7, name groups 13 and 16), so one must be registered
the criterion's name and users list are not fixed by the request or policy and are not tested

disagreement: source: one pass names the criterion check alone, the other also the HR service check; chose both because the service check requires the linked criterion to be an active case_visibility criterion for HR Service Desk, which only this requirement tests

requirements.text: Provide the current list of cases tied to HR Account Access Request
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_service IN (4, 5) AND assignment_group = 4
assumptions: boundary of the case selector: cases 4 and 58 (HR Accounts Inquiry, 'Inquiry about HR account permissions') and 5 and 59 (HR Portal Support Request, 'Support needed for HR Portal navigation') have near-matching service names and HR portal descriptions but are not tied to HR Account Access Request, so none is rerouted to HR Service Desk

disagreement: selector: one pass covers services 4 and 5 and counts their cases outside HR Service Desk (expected 4), the other covers service 4 only and counts its cases in HR Service Desk (expected 0); chose both services because the request's 'through the HR portal' would sweep in the portal-support cases, and the zero count because rerouting to HR Service Desk is what the boundary forbids

case_visibility_criteria_exists_for_hr_s.evidence: the query joins any user group, so the four active case_visibility criteria on the seed (1, 5, 6 and 7, for groups 13 and 16) already satisfy it; its own description and the request name the HR Service Desk population, so the criterion must name user_group 4

hr_service_has_case_visibility_applied.evidence: the query accepts any active case_visibility criterion, so linking the existing criterion for group 13 would pass; its description names the criterion created for the HR Service Desk and the request restricts the service to that population, so the linked criterion must be the new one for user_group 4

no_hr_account_access_cases_misclassified.evidence: both cases tied to the service (3 and 57) already have coe_type HRIT on the seed, so the count is 0 before the agent acts

notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: that the rerouted cases' assignees belong to HR Service Desk; one pass has it, the other left the assignee untested; kept because the policy requires the assigned user to be a current member of the case's assignment group, the request names that group, and neither current assignee (users 5 and 9) is a member. Its disjunctive cell (empty or a member) is rewritten as a count of cases whose assignee is outside the group, expected 0, which an empty assignee also satisfies (resolved on that requirement).
disagreement: value: the source of the criterion requirement: one pass lists the criterion check alone, the other adds the HR service check; chose both, since the service check requires the linked criterion to be an active case_visibility criterion, which only that requirement tests (resolved on that requirement).
disagreement: value: the boundary stay on near-named services: one pass covers HR Accounts Inquiry and HR Portal Support Request and counts their cases outside HR Service Desk (expected 4), the other covers HR Accounts Inquiry only and counts its cases in HR Service Desk (expected 0); chose both services with the zero count (resolved on that requirement).
The passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id and cell; their texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
The acting user, Karen Watkins (user 39), holds the admin role. The policy bars administrators from routine HR case work and lists reassigning cases across groups under the HR Manager role; the request makes rerouting the misrouted cases part of the configuration fix and the benchmark expects it, so the case requirements stand, though a reviewer may judge the rerouting a policy conflict.
Providing the list of cases is a reply and leaves no database state. The new criterion's name and its users column are not tested: the request fixes neither, and users is a JSON column that is empty on every criterion in the seed, so its storage format is not shown.
